CITY OF SAN MARINO

  DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA

 Howard Brody, Chair  www.cityofsanmarino.org

 Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair  (626) 300-0711 Phone

 Joyce Gatsoulis-Batnij  2200 Huntington Drive

  WEDNESDAY, MAY 1, 2019
  7:00 P.M.
  CITY HALL
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE, SAN MARINO, CA

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Design Review Committee
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of every month.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a modification
or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 300-0705
at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Chair Howard Brody, Vice-Chair Kevin Cheng, Committee Member Judy Johnson-
  Brody, Committee Member Chris Huang, Committee Member Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij,
  and Alternate Committee Member Ben Lundgren

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200 Huntington
Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive and the Recreation Department, 1560 Pasqualito
Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s Website: http://www.cityofsanmarino.org

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the Design
Review Committee on any item of interest to the public, before or during the Design Review Committee’s
consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Design Review Committee.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – MAY 1, 2019  PAGE 2 OF 3

  2. DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC19-1

  (Required Action Date: 6-3-19)

  3. DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC19-10

  The applicant proposes to construct a second story addition and exterior modifications to the existing
  two-story residence.
  (Required Action Date: 6-14-19)

  4. DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC17-54
  979 ROXBURY RD., (WANG/LAI)
  The applicant proposes to construct a first and second story addition to the existing two-story residence.
  (Required Action Date: 6-10-19)

  OTHER MATTERS

  5. CONSIDERATION OF PELLA LIFESTYLE SERIES WINDOW MATERIAL FOR THE PRE-APPROVED
  WINDOW MATERIAL LIST.

  6. DISCUSSION ON THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA).

OPEN FORUM

This is an opportunity for future applicants to informally present preliminary design concepts for feedback from
members of the DRC. Comments received are based on members not having visited the site and neighborhood.
Therefore, positive comments should not be perceived as preliminary approval of a project but rather as a tool
in facilitating a project through the Design Review process. No more than two DRC members may participate
in Open Forum discussions. Applications that have been heard by the DRC may not be discussed during Open
Forum.

PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

All public writings distributed by the City of San Marino to at least a majority of the Design Review Committee
regarding any item on this agenda will be made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200
Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – MAY 1, 2019  PAGE 3 OF 3

ADJOURNMENT

The San Marino Design Review Committee will adjourn to the next regular meeting to be held on Wednesday,
May 15, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.

APPEALS

There is a fifteen day appeal period for all applications. All appeals should be filed with the Planning and Building
Department. Please contact the Planning and Building Department for further information.

TO:  Chair Brody and Members of the Design Review Committee

FROM:  Christine Song, Assistant Planner
DATE:  May 1, 2019
SUBJECT:  MODIFICATION TO DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC14-45
  2131 S. OAK KNOLL AVE., (ZHANG/TTL CONSTRUCTION, INC.)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to modify the roofing product of a previously approved project to a
roofing product color that is not on the City’s Pre-Approved Roof Materials Colors and
Application List. The applicant requests to install the Boral two-piece mission clay tile roofing
material in the Carmel Blend color. Design Review Case No. DRC14-45 was previously
approved on August 20, 2014.

This is an after the fact approval request, as the project contractor has already purchased the
Boral roofing material and a portion of the product has already been loaded on the roof.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

May 1, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
June 14, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 3
Object – 0
Neither - 1
 No response – 7

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

In addition to the required findings, the Code allows the DRC to consider the following items
when reviewing a roof material applications: 1. Fire, wind and/or earthquake safety; 2. Structural
integrity; 3. The extent the roof is exposed to public view or view by neighbors; and 4. The
ability of the proposed roofing material to successfully dispose of rainwater for the particular
house.

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐ YES  ☒NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The legal neighborhood consists of homes in various traditional styles. If
  the proposed change in roofing material and color were approved, the Mediterranean
  style structure would not be compatible with the legal neighborhood. The Spanish style
  homes in the vicinity are somewhat comparable to the Mediterranean style of the
  proposed structure in terms of roof style and those properties are improved with the
  traditional red mission clay tile roofing material.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which
  balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous
  properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property
  within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☐NO  ☒NOT APPLICABLE

  3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐ YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: Although the proposed modification is not a building addition, the change in
  roof material and color would not be compatible with the Mediterranean style of the
  structure (which is currently in construction). The proposed color and style of the
  roofing product would result in a more contemporary appearance, which deviates from
  the previously approved traditional design intention of the project.

  2
 4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or
  structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed Boral tile in the Carmel Blend color would not be consistent
  with the Mediterranean style of the structure as it is not a compatible selection for the
  project. The proposed earth tone blend of the roofing material is in stark contrast to
  the previously approved reclaimed French terra cotta roof tile in a red blend color,
  which had a rustic and aged quality. The proposed Carmel blend color would be better
  suited for a home with more modern characteristics.

  3
        Howard Brody, Chair
  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  Ben Lundgren, Alternate

TO:  Chair Brody and Members of the Design Review Committee

FROM:  Christine Song, Assistant Planner
DATE:  May 1, 2019
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC19-1
  2730 LOMBARDY RD., (COPELAND)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to install exterior modifications to the existing one-story residence,
which includes replacing the existing lattice support column with a new wood column at the
front entry and replacing an existing window along the front elevation.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

May 1, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
June 3, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 5
Object – 0
No response – 7

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:
 1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The legal neighborhood is characterized by mostly one-story homes in
  Minimal Traditional styles. The proposed changes are minimal; the new wood support
  column and new wood window are still in keeping with the Minimal Traditional style of
  the home and will not cause any compatibility issues with the legal neighborhood.

2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which
  balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous
  properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property
  within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The new wood window would be replacing an existing window and would
  be smaller in size. No privacy impacts are anticipated from this change.

3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: There is no building addition proposed as part of this project. The proposed
  changes will still be consistent with the style of the existing home.

4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or
  structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The color of the new wood post and the new window will match the white
  color of the existing windows (Sherwood Williams – Snowbound). The applicant is
  proposing to repaint the existing structure (Sherwood Williams – Gray Clouds) and
  staff finds that the color selection is a suitable choice.

  2
    Howard Brody, Chair
  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  Ben Lundgren, Alternate

TO:  Chair Brody and Members of the Design Review Committee
FROM:  Christine Song, Assistant Planner
DATE:  May 1, 2019
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC19-10
  1675 WEST DR., (SUMMER GARDEN LIMITED/CHELSEA DESIGN &
  CONSTRUCTION)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a second-story addition and exterior modifications to the
existing two-story residence.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

PROJECT HISTORY

May 1, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
June 14, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 5
Object – 0
Neither – 1
No response – 7

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:
 1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The legal neighborhood consists of one and two-story structures in various
  architectural styles. There are slight changes proposed to the front of the existing
  structure and the modifications will not affect the current compatibility of the structure
  with the neighborhood. The proposed improvements will provide a nice update to the
  existing streetscape and help restore the appearance of the project site.

2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner which
  balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on contiguous
  properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to develop their property
  within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed balcony on the second floor would face the San Marino
  School District administrative office along the north elevation and would not pose any
  major privacy impacts. Along the south elevation, the balcony would face the adjacent
  neighbor’s garage structure and would not disturb any reasonable expectation of
  privacy. The new and replacement windows along the north and south elevations would
  not significantly intensify any visibility into neighboring structures.

3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing building
  which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The project proposes a small addition to the second story to expand the
  existing master bedroom amenities and restore an unpermitted enclosed balcony, while
  adding necessary exterior modifications. Staff finds that these improvements would help
  enhance the existing structure by re-introducing traditional Spanish style characteristics
  to the property.

4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or
  structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒ YES  ☐ NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: All proposed colors and materials will match those that are currently
  existing on the structure. New and replacement windows will use natural wood
  material which is allowed on the City’s Pre-Approved Window Material List.

  2
    Howard Brody, Chair
  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  Ben Lundgren, Alternate

TO:  Chair Brody and Members of the Design Review Committee

FROM:  Eva Choi, Associate Planner
DATE:  May 1, 2019
SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC17-54
  979 ROXBURY DR., (WANG/LAI)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct a first and second-story addition and remodel to an existing
two-story structure.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) because the project involves an existing structure.

PROJECT HISTORY

May 1, 2019 – First hearing before the DRC
June 10, 2019 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 6
Object – 2
No response – 5

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application if
it finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.
   Staff can make this finding:  ☒YES  ☐ NO ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The project involves adding a study directly above the street-facing garage and
  extending the first and second floors along the east side yard. Majority of the structures
  within the legal neighborhood have a two-story façade and the proposal would not alter
  the streetscape or render the structure incompatible with the neighborhood.

2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner
  which balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on
  contiguous properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to
  develop their property within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: New windows for the addition project will not provide a direct sightline into
  the adjacent structures. An uncovered balcony on the second floor is accessed from the
  loft area and from a spiral staircase leading to the rear yard. Staff was unable to find similar
  outdoor living features in the neighborhood. Additionally, the large uncovered balcony has
  the potential to cause privacy intrusion and noise impact on adjacent properties. Staff
  recommends removal of the balcony and spiral staircase from the project.

3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing
  building which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The addition project provides consistent plate height and roof slope as the
  existing structure. There is a small portion of flat roof over the loft area and this is not
  visible from the street. The addition over the garage follows the same building articulation
  as the first floor with the garage projecting towards the street.

4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building or
  structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed exterior colors and materials are consistent with the existing
  structure. There are existing wood shutters fronting Roxbury Drive, the designer is
  proposing to provide matching shutters on the new window above the garage. Although
  the shutters are not functional, staff found the existing shutters undersized in width and
  recommends providing shutter that equals half of the window opening similar to shutters
  found on the immediate adjacent structures. Staff also recommends that the project
  provides consistent window treatments, including the provision of window sills.

  2
 3
      Howard Brody, Chair
  Kevin Cheng, Vice-Chair
  Judy Johnson-Brody
  Chris Huang
  Joyce Gatsoulis Batnij
  Ben Lundgren, Alternate

TO:  Chair Brody and Members of the Design Review Committee

FROM:  Christine Song, Assistant Planner
DATE:  May 1, 2019
SUBJECT:  CONSIDERATION OF PELLA LIFESTYLE WINDOW PRODUCT FOR
  THE PRE-APPROVED WINDOW MATERIAL LIST

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant requests that the DRC consider the Pella Lifestyle aluminum clad window
material series for recommendation to the Planning Commission for inclusion on the City’s
Pre-Approved Window Material List. This is the first time that the Pella Lifestyle window line is
being presented to the DRC for consideration.

The applicant was not able to identify any properties where the Lifestyle windows have been
installed within the city of San Marino, as this product line is still fairly new to the Pella brand.

A representative from Pella will be present at the meeting to provide a presentation, show
product samples, and answer questions about the Lifestyle window product. In addition to the
product brochure that has been provided, product information can be found on the company’s
website at https://www.pella.com/windows/lifestyle-series/.

The inclusion of this product on the City’s Pre-Approved List would mean that the product can
be installed on a home without a public hearing by the DRC. However, the window
replacement permit application would still be reviewed by staff before the City issues a building
permit. The staff-level review ensures that the new windows’ style, grid system, color,
operation, and other design details match the existing windows and are compatible with the
style of the home.
